Baseline: main `8ef9aa5a4` (#168), audited on 2026-09-26. This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec. Corrections implemented locally are labeled and remain unshipped until merged. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. The earlier isolated run passed 6 identity, 5 schema-guard, 10 release-command and 14 durable-release tests. Those tests do not establish the missing producer/consumer or ecosystem coverage. No full `just ci`, hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run was performed in that audit.

## Implemented locally, awaiting merge

These corrections are not shipped. [Batch verification](V1-VERIFICATION.md) records local results and remaining checks.

| Finding | Correction and evidence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-ENV | Unchanged decide stdout reproduced E281 at the baseline. The CLI accepts the decide report or strict bare wire while preserving typed validation. Review also found strict post-move verification rejected the action's own update with E148; the model now permits only that exact applied-head transition. Real-binary, model and shell action tests cover the boundaries and unrelated-change negatives. | T01 | REL-PR-02, REL-PR-04, REL-PR-07 |
| SYS-INSTALL | Auto installation honors explicit/action-ref versions, including inside Callisto source. Local compilation requires explicit source selection and native workspace ownership checks. Isolated installer fixtures cover consumer names, pins, source rejection and attestation/fallback behavior. | T11 | REL-PR-06 |
| SYS-SCHEMA | Custom string serializers now have string-shaped, named schema definitions. A full JSON Schema validator checks every exposed schema target against real report/durable payloads and malformed nested values; full CI passes. | T02 | CLI-SCHEMA-01, CLI-OUT-05, REL-CMD-12 |
| SYS-PYDEC | Durable release entries, operations, slots and bound registry observations decode versions with the owning distribution's grammar. Genuine Python stable release plan/execute/rerun tests preserve PEP 440 values and reject foreign rosters; independent review found no must-fix. | T03 | REL-AUTH-01/03 |
| SYS-CASCADE | Dependency declarations now retain both local key and native target; graph walking and shared cascade/floor/snapshot rewriting use the declaration's manifest ecosystem. Cargo aliases, inherited root declarations, promoted dual Cargo/npm packages and normalized Python graph names have regressions; independent review cleared T04 and full CI passes. | T04 | VER-CAS-07, VER-PRE-09 |
| SYS-PYPRE | Pre-release baselines now resolve their historical/display identity before native grammar validation. Validation uses the original JSON spelling, so PEP 440 fallback cannot normalize invalid SemVer input; Python stable cycles, promoted/historical keys, malformed values, exit and resume are covered. | T03-PRE | VER-PRE-01/03/06/10 |
| SYS-INHERITED, SYS-ROOT | Historical release verification now reads effective versions from Git blobs, including Cargo workspace inheritance; normalized root/member/changelog paths are checked against the claimed roster. Tests cover authority-only root changes, unclaimed owners and unsafe paths. | T03-HISTORY | REL-AUTH-02, VER-APPLY-13 |
| SYS-PNPM | Dependency state now retains pnpm workspace suffixes, alias targets and relative paths. Explicit SemVer ranges are checked and safely rewritten; aliases preserve keys, relative references resolve only to admitted members, and native pack/frozen-install tests cover version and snapshot flows. | T04-PNPM | WS-ID-10, VER-CAS-05/06 |
| SYS-LOCK | Lockfile refresh and staging now include every actual version/dependency/platform/optional-dependency write ecosystem, including dual manifests and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cross-ecosystem and dependency-only regressions pass in full CI. | T04-LOCK | VER-APPLY-14, VER-PRE-08 |
| SYS-VERSION-RECOVERY | Consumed changesets and pre-state deletions are deferred until lock refresh and generated-state staging succeed. Partial-run detection checks staged effective versions, permits metadata-only edits and handles the examined prerelease exit and inherited-Cargo cases; regressions cover untracked inputs, failed deletion staging, staged/restored versions, exit-state stable bumps, and a fresh E121 refusal after pre-state deletion staging fails. | T05 | VER-APPLY-08/10/13/15/16 |
| SYS-BINS, SYS-NONCARGO | Cargo executable discovery covers explicit and automatic bin targets. npm/Python executables are rejected as unsupported generated artifact builders before writes, while registry-only setup remains available. Focused init and manifest tests plus full CI pass. | T10-BINS | CLI-INIT-01/02/12, CLI-WF-04 |
| SYS-AUTH | Generated release actions configure npm auth in a mode-0600 temporary user config using `${NPM_TOKEN}` interpolation (the secret is not written to disk), map PyPI credentials to Twine, support Bun's token contract, and filter release credentials including `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from Python build subprocesses. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain normal package-owner-defined behavior; Callisto does not suppress or rewrite them. Fake-tool and environment-filter tests pass; generated workflow tests keep secrets out of version-pr/plan/build. | T10-AUTH | CLI-WF-03/04; ADR 4 |

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-OWNER | `sole_owner_at`: current first-manifest path existence is not historic name/full-roster ownership. Reproduced loss of a bare tag after sibling rename or addition of a new primary canonical manifest. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-DEMOTION | `tags.rs`: removing a same-named sibling loses a newer qualified tag and chooses an older bare release. Reproduced; inference can replay already-released work. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-RETRY | `derive_unreleased_decision`: local tags exclude a package before remaining operations are observed. Reproduced tag creation followed by push failure, then exit 0 with `Nothing to release.` and no receipt. Generated simple CI uses this path; Callisto's own committed-roster CI does not. | T08-RETRY | REL-RERUN-02; REL-CMD-01/08 need coordinated selection changes |
| SYS-BARRIER | `release/derive.rs`: a dual Cargo/npm owner creates a shared physical tag/GitHub publication after one distribution but before the other's publish. Reproduced plan ordering; per-distribution gates do not enforce the owner's completion barrier. | T08 | REL-ORD-01 |
| SYS-NAPI | `commands/init.rs`: generated native builds and placement use workspace-wide napi selection rather than the verified intent. An unrelated addon can block a Cargo-only release. Source-confirmed. | T10 | CLI-WF-04; committed roster authority |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYFILES | `provider/registry.rs` returns Exact for any matching non-yanked Python file; `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as AlreadySatisfied. `registry_argv.rs` builds both wheel and sdist. Source-confirmed partial-upload retry gap; no live fault-injection run yet. | T09 | REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04 |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

## v0.9 handoff

Merge the verified T01 correction to unblock release-PR refresh. Then require fresh release-source/decision agreement and passing workflow checks before merging the refreshed PR; do not merge the stale #113 decision as a workaround. [Run 36281315129](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/36281315129) records the E281 failure that prevented refresh after later merges. No claim that E281 is the only possible publication blocker is established until the actual self-release succeeds.

The publication intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files are written without the stdout report envelope, so the same wrapper mismatch was not found there. That source inspection does not replace executing the publish path.

crates/callisto-cli/CHANGELOG.md  55.7K
# callisto-cli

## 0.10.2

- Releases that ship artifacts no longer fail with E140: the GitHub CLI that checks attestations and publishes the release keeps its own token instead of running unauthenticated.

## 0.10.1

- Generated npm and PyPI releases configure native registry authentication for publishing without exposing credentials to Python build backends.
- GitHub Actions honor requested Callisto versions; building checkout source requires source: local.
- Versioning refreshes and stages lockfiles for every package manifest and dependency declaration it updates, including dual Cargo and npm packages.
- Release decisions verify effective package versions from the selected commit, including versions inherited from Cargo workspace metadata, and only treat direct-child changeset Markdown files (excluding README.md) as consumed changesets.
- Interrupted version runs retain release inputs until generated changes and their removal are safely staged, prevent unsafe retries, and explain how to inspect staged work and finish recovery.
- Version and snapshot updates recognize Cargo aliases and equivalent Python distribution names while preserving dependency declaration spelling.
- CLI JSON schemas accurately describe the string values emitted for versions, package identities, and digests.
- Pre-release baselines are validated using each package's native version syntax, including when packages share a name or have been promoted to ecosystem-qualified ids.
- npm version ranges with `||` alternatives are understood for dependency coverage; pnpm workspace aliases, relative references and explicit ranges are resolved and updated without changing their protocol or dependency names.
- Python dependencies pinned in `[project.optional-dependencies]` extras are now followed: bumping a package releases the packages that pin it in an extra and rewrites the pin, instead of leaving stale published metadata.
- Durable release plans read Python package versions using PEP 440 semantics.
- The release PR refreshes reliably when the forge is slow to show the moved branch, instead of failing with E148 after the branch has already been updated.
- Generated artifact workflows include every supported Cargo binary; npm and Python executables remain registry releases unless a custom workflow builds their artifacts. `callisto init` now reports E304 when an npm or Python executable is chosen as the product
- Cargo dependencies declared under `[target.<cfg>.dependencies]` are now followed: bumping a package releases its target-specific dependents and rewrites their pins, instead of leaving a stale pin that broke the workspace.
- Automated release PRs can refresh using generated decisions without rejecting their own branch updates.

## 0.10.0

- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger`, fixed groups, linked groups, the tag template and pre-major inference as configured when you set them, instead of "(default)".
- `snapshot` works for PyPI packages: their snapshot version and dependents' specs use PEP 440.
- Git errors that came from parsing git's own output now have specific codes and help text, instead of one generic git error code.
- release, release plan, release execute, release artifact-manifest, and release-pr's JSON output now carry schemaVersion, command, and dryRun fields like every other command's JSON output.
- `callisto release-pr verify` accepts `callisto release-pr decide --format json` output as-is again, so the release action can open and update the release PR. 0.9.0 failed with E281.
- Adding a package with the same name in another ecosystem needs no configuration: the existing package keeps its release history, tags and changelog, and new tags use the qualified name (`cargo/foo@1.1.0`). A pre-release cycle started before the new package k
- init now names the exact file it failed to write when a write fails, instead of a pathless error.
- In pre-release mode, packages with the same name in two ecosystems (`cargo/foo`, `npm/foo`) keep separate starting versions in `pre.json` instead of sharing one.
- `callisto release` no longer fails with E167 when GitHub is slow to show a release or asset it just created, uploaded or published; it waits up to a minute.

## 0.9.0

- callisto release --dry-run and callisto release plan now include a diagnostics array in their JSON output when an artifact owner package is selected without its product package, instead of only printing a stderr warning.
- callisto version now refreshes npm, pnpm, yarn, bun and pdm lockfiles by default (in addition to Cargo, uv and poetry), opt out with --no-refresh-lockfiles; a failed refresh now stops the command with a coded error naming the lockfile and command
- A dependent released in the same run has its spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the new version, even when the old spec still covers it.
- Generated release workflows pass the detected default branch to the release-PR action, and `init` now resolves it from a live remote query or the checked-out branch when `origin/HEAD` isn't set locally, instead of silently defaulting to `main`.
- **Git runs through the system `git` binary only**
  
  The in-process gitoxide backend is gone; every Git read and write already had to work through the `git` binary the CLI requires. Commit inference keeps a commit that touched a package even when a later merge discarded its change (`git log --full-history`), m
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_model::vcs` (was `callisto-vcs`): removed `GitRepository`, `ShellGit`, the `GitDataSource` trait and the revwalk visit counter. `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` is now `GitAccess::new(root, runner)` with inherent methods.
  - `callisto_model::vcs`: `commits_since` with an unresolvable `since` ref returns `VcsError::RefNotFound` (was `VcsError::Git` from the shell path).
- Shell completions no longer offer hidden plumbing subcommands, at any nesting depth
- snapshot rewrites every dependency spec the snapshot version falls outside of, so cargo metadata resolves after a snapshot
- Loading a workspace now fails with a clear error naming both directories when two of them declare the same ecosystem and name, instead of silently routing dependency edges to the wrong package.
- Fixed groups compute their shared version from the highest member version when no member is tagged, support PEP 440 versions, and follow pre-release mode. Before, an untagged group could be bumped down to 0.x.
- `callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`
  
  `callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the
- Workspace discovery no longer silently drops or misattaches packages: a manifest that fails to parse now fails with a clear error naming the path when it's a real workspace member, and warns otherwise; root detection asks git itself instead of hand-walking f
- Every add/version/schema/pre/release-pr error now carries its own code and help text instead of a generic message; release-pr decide/verify report the exact invalid-branch or duplicate-pull-request code instead of a plain string when reading a snapshot or de
- callisto init and callisto release --dry-run in a repository without an origin remote no longer print a stray git error about the missing remote.
- **`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**
  
  `init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resultin
  
  Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `ve
  
  Breaking:
  - `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
  - A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
  - `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
  - Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.

# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state

Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)

## Context

- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).

## Decision

Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).

## Options considered

- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).

## Consequences

- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). Local tag-filtered selection can still discard unfinished push/forge work before execution, and Python version observation does not establish complete file-set publication; both are tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Enforcement

- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.

## Revisit when

- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".

content.content:
# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset means informational only; `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`,
# so a CI coverage failure always reproduces locally with the same invocation.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Check per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%). The
# workspace-total --fail-under-lines gate can pass while a small crate is
# far below threshold, since a few large crates dominate the total line
# count -- this catches that case. Requires profile data from a prior
# `cargo llvm-cov` run in this session (e.g. `just coverage` just ran, or
# CI's own coverage step ran first); does not re-run tests itself.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:

# V1 implementation and stacked-PR execution

Status: active execution portfolio. Baseline: `origin/main` at `0a971b211` (#172); the work branch carries local T01/T11 commits `20ce30cd1`, `a37025927` and `f4ce5f22d`, with earlier documentation reconciliation preserved in the dirty worktree. [Task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Execution status: the branch contains T01 producer/consumer and unchanged-applied-head commits (`20ce30cd1`, `f4ce5f22d`) and the independent T11 installer commit (`a37025927`). T02, T03, T03-PRE, T03-HISTORY, T04, T04-PNPM, T04-LOCK, T05, T10-BINS and T10-AUTH remain implemented in the worktree. On 2026-09-28, all 1,861 Nextest tests passed and line coverage reached 93.44%; the aggregate `just ci` recipe still exits at the sandbox-protected cargo-deny advisory lock, while the offline audit passes with authorized cache access. Docs, workflow contracts, zizmor, release behavior and the 90% coverage gate also pass individually. The owner-approved T05 policy is fail-closed E121 with manual recovery guidance; no automatic deletion or persisted checkpoint is added. The local `pr/v1-current-contract` pointer exists, but no PR has been opened remotely. Architectural D01 choices, remote delivery and publication remain separate decisions.

## PR-sized lanes and current position

| Lane | PR-sized units | Dependency or constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release/wire | T01 producer/consumer fix → T02 schema repair → T03 contextual decisions → T03-PRE baselines; T03-HISTORY inherited/root verification follows T03 and T04 | T01 fix is committed; other units local; stack separation remains |
| Native resolution | T04 manifest-local names → T04-PNPM protocols → T04-LOCK refresh | Implemented locally; review corrections closed; stack separation remains |
| Installer | T11 version/source fidelity | Committed locally as `a37025927`; independent review and combined full CI pass |
| Early workflows | T10-BINS binary inventory/unsupported builders → T10-AUTH native auth | Both implemented locally; docs preserve owner-controlled native hooks, which retain their normal environment |

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use Git worktrees and native GitHub stacks.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from a dirty shared checkout.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); plain chained PRs targeting a parent branch get no CI because `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` triggers only for PRs targeting `main`. Each
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git reba
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a chil

Create or update a stack on GitHub from branch names, PR numbers, or PR URLs.

This command does not rely on gh-stack local tracking state. It is
designed for users who manage branches with external tools (e.g. jj,

PRs without adopting local stack tracking.

those PRs are used. For branches without PRs, new PRs are created
automatically with the correct base branch chaining.

content.content:
- uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {mode: version-pr, branch: __BRANCH__}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.decision.outputs.release }}
      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      has_napi: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.has_napi }}
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      # Content precondition, not release detection: `release plan` requires this commit to write its decision.
      - name: Check for a release decision
        id: decision
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release=false
          if git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^ > /dev/null &&
            git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only --diff-filter=AM -r HEAD^ HEAD | grep -qxF .callisto/release-decision.json; then
            release=true
          fi
          echo "release=$release" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      - name: Plan the release
        if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent"
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
      - name: Build the matrix from napi targets and artifact slots
        id: matrix
        if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          report="$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json"
          callisto --format json matrix > "$report"
          napi=$(jq -c '[.platformTargets[] | select(.kind=="napi") | .targets[] | {kind: "napi"} + .]' "$report")
          slots=$(jq -c --slurpfile report "$report" '[.artifactSlots[] as $slot
            | ([$report[0].platformTargets[] | select(.kind=="cargo") | .targets[]
                | select(.artifactName == $slot.assetName and .triple == $slot.platform)] | first
              // error("callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot \($slot.assetName)"))
            | {kind: "cargo"} + .]' "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          {
            echo "matrix=$(jq -cn --argjson napi "$napi" --argjson slots "$slots" '$napi + $slots')"
            echo "has_napi=$(jq 'length > 0' <<< "$napi")"
            echo "has_artifacts=$(jq 'length > 0' <<< "$slots")"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix != '[]'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.hostRunner }}
    permissions: {contents: read, id-token: write, attestations: write}
    env:
      KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
      TRIPLE: ${{ matrix.triple }}
      USE_CROSS: ${{ matrix.useCross }}
      PACKAGE_DIR: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
      PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.packageName }}
      MANIFEST_PATH: ${{ matrix.manifestPath }}
      ASSET: ${{ matrix.artifactName }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {persist-credentials: false}
      - name: Install the Rust target
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rustup target add "$TRIPLE"
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then cargo install cross --locked --version 0.2.5; fi
      - name: Build the napi addon
        if: matrix.kind == 'napi'
        run: |
          if-no-files-found: error

  execute:
    needs: [plan, build]
    # A skipped build blocks only when the matrix had entries to build.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix == '[]'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: callisto-release-execute, cancel-in-progress: false}
    permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0} # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: napi-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
      - name: Place napi artifacts
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto --format json matrix \
            | jq -r '[.platformTargets[] | select(.kind=="napi") | .targets[].packageDir] | unique[]' \
            | while IFS= read -r dir; do
              npx --yes --package @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4 napi artifacts --cwd "${dir:-.}" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-artifacts"
            done
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: asset-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets
      - name: Write the artifact manifest
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify permissions that GitHub only enforces when a guarded release path is
# actually exercised. Keeping this separate from the generic action-pin check
# makes the release authority contract visible and testable on every PR.
set -euo pipefail

workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml

job_block() {
  local job="$1" next_job="$2"
  sed -n "/^  ${job}:$/,/^  ${next_job}:$/p" "$workflow"
}

require_line() {
  local block="$1" expected="$2" description="$3"
  if ! grep -Fqx "$expected" <<< "$block"; then
    printf 'release workflow contract failed: %s\n' "$description" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

version_pr="$(job_block version-pr plan)"
require_line "$version_pr" '      contents: write' 'version-pr must write the managed branch'
require_line "$version_pr" '      pull-requests: write' 'version-pr must create or update the release PR'
require_line "$version_pr" "          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'" 'version-pr must refresh Cargo.lock for coupled Cargo version bumps; the action appends its single authoritative --emit-decision argument'

action=.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh
if ! rg -Fqx 'command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")' "$action"; then
  printf 'release workflow contract failed: release-PR action must append the exact decision path once\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

release_candidate="$(job_block release-candidate version-pr)"
require_line "$release_candidate" '          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '\''[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'\''"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'\''" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length'\'')' 'release-candidate must validate an explicit source only when it is a merged managed branch'
require_line "$release_candidate" '          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}' 'release-candidate must pass a dispatch input through an environment variable'
require_line "$release_candidate" '          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}' 'release-candidate must pass the triggering commit through an environment variable'
require_line "$release_candidate" '          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"' 'release-candidate must not interpolate user-controlled SHA input into shell'

build_artifact="$(job_block build-artifact build)"
require_line "$build_artifact" '      contents: read' 'each target build must read the intent-bound source tree'
require_line "$build_artifact" '      attestations: write' 'each target build must create provenance attestations'
require_line "$build_artifact" '      id-token: write' 'each target build must mint the Sigstore OIDC identity'
require_line "$build_artifact" '          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent' 'each target build must keep the release handoff outside either checkout'
require_line "$build_artifact" '          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}' 'each target build must attest its staged artifact bytes'
require_line "$build_artifact" '          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh' 'production artifact builds must use the shared preflighted build recipe'
require_line "$build_artifact" '            target: aarch64-apple-darwin' 'the product matrix must build macOS ARM64'
require_line "$build_artifact" '            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu' 'the product matrix must build glibc Linux x86_64'
require_line "$build_artifact" '            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl' 'the product matrix must build musl Linux x86_64'

build="$(job_block build execute)"
require_line "$build" '          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"' 'assembly must create the exact three-slot artifact manifest'

plan="$(job_block plan build-artifact)"
require_line "$plan" '          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}' 'planning must use one resolved current orchestration revision'
require_line "$plan" '          path: release-source' 'planning must check out the explicit release source separately'
require_line "$plan" '          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}' 'planning must pass the coordinator revision through an environment variable'
require_line "$plan" '            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \' 'planning must bind the current coordinator without shell interpolation'
require_line "$plan" '            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \' 'planning must bind the exact release source checkout'

execute="$(sed -n '/^  execute:$/,$p' "$workflow")"

- Addon in the release next to an unrelated one: only the released addon is built and placed.

`derive_release_inputs_with` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs` was one 400-line function. It is now a short sequence of named stages over an `Ops` value (the operations and prepared operations built so far) and an `OpIndex` (the per-package publish, platform, tag, forge and upload indexes later stages read their prerequisites from): select packages, prepare the remote, build publish leaves, link publish prerequisites, add tags, add forge releases, add artifact uploads, add forge publishes.

Moves only. The statements are the original ones, called in the original order, because the intent digest covers the operations and a reordering would change every durable intent. The only edits are borrows (`&selected` to `selected`) and the destructuring of `Ops`.

Two commits:
- Characterization first: snapshots of the package inputs, ordered operations, prepared operations and artifact slots for a Cargo chain, a product release with a plugin artifact, an npm owner with platform packages, a scoped npm prerelease and a dual Cargo and npm owner (commit hashes and the checkout path redacted), plus four error paths the line-coverage report showed unexecuted: an entry the workspace does not contain, a product without its artifact owner, a forge repository other than origin, a duplicate registry target. The remaining uncovered lines are internal invariants that cannot be reached.
- The split. The snapshots pass unchanged.

Verification: dropping the platform prerequisites from the link stage fails the npm-owner snapshot and the existing platform test. `just ci` passes. No changeset: no behavior change.

First of two PRs in lane D: SYS-BARRIER follows on top of this.

input.content:
fix(release): resume a tagged release together with its untagged dependencies

An independent review of the rerun fix found cases it got wrong. Operations run dependents first, so a failed push can leave only a dependent's tag behind; the rerun then derived a roster of just that package and failed with E169 on its untagged dependency. The observation now plans the roster a run would (untagged packages plus the tagged-on-HEAD ones) and observes only the tagged packages' operations. A preview with no origin cannot observe, so it keeps tagged releases in the plan instead of reporting nothing to release while the run fails. Only the tag the current template would create counts as the release's tag.

Reading a local tag no longer parses its message, so a tag with several paragraphs or a signature is adopted as the same landed effect instead of failing as malformed output. The resume tests use an offline runner so they never contact a real remote.

input.content:
Follow-up to #202 from an independent review of it. #202 merged before these fixes landed.

Fixed:
- A tagged dependent is resumed together with its untagged dependency. Operations run dependents first, so a failed push can leave only a dependent's tag behind. The rerun derived a roster of just that package and failed with E169 on its untagged dependency, which is worse than before #202. The observation now plans the roster a run would (untagged packages plus the tagged-on-HEAD ones) and observes only the tagged packages' operations.
- A preview with no `origin` cannot observe, so it keeps tagged releases in the plan. Before, it reported "Nothing to release." while the real run failed for lack of a remote.
- A local tag whose message has several paragraphs or a signature is adopted. Reading the tag parsed its body and rejected anything non-empty as malformed output, against ADR 9 and REL-RERUN-02 (annotation text is never compared). Only the object type is read now.
- Only the tag the current template would create counts as the release's tag; one made under an older template no longer makes the package look released and then get a second tag.
- The resume tests use an offline runner. The earlier test contacted a real GitHub URL and, offline, sat through the retry sleeps.

Tests, each failing before its fix: a dependent tagged at HEAD with an untagged dependency (preview and run), the no-origin preview, and a multi-paragraph tag message. `just ci` passes. Changeset for the tag message.

Known and left as is, from the same review:
- A hand-made lightweight tag at HEAD for a finished release now fails with E167 until the next commit, as REL-RERUN-03 says a lightweight tag is never adopted.
- A preview with credentials or network missing keeps the package in the plan, since an observation that fails counts as not satisfied. The run reports the real error.
- Observation runs for every tagged-on-HEAD package even with `--package`, and offline it waits through the retry schedule per operation.

content.text:
The stack conflict is resolved, and I opened #211 to carry the review fixes for #202. `just ci` passes on every branch tip I touched.

**Stack conflict**
- **Cause:** #202 merged and edited a test inside the block that #205 moves out of `init.rs`.
- **Fix:** I merged `main` into the bottom branch, kept the split `init.rs` and carried the two-line test edit into `init/tests.rs`. Then I merged upward through #206 and #208. There were no force-pushes.
- **Now:** #205, #206, #208, #209 and #204 all show mergeable.
- **Merged since last report:** #202 and #203 are merged. The pending release PR is #210.

**Review of #202**
- I had an agent review it independently. It found defects, so I opened #211 off `main`, since #202 had already merged. The first two below were each red before the fix.
- **E169 on rerun:** operations run dependents first, so a failed push can leave only a dependent's tag. The rerun then failed with E169 on its untagged dependency, which is worse than before #202. It now resumes the dependent together with the dependency.
- **Multi-paragraph and signed tags:** these failed as malformed output. They are now adopted, as ADR 9 requires.
- **No-`origin` preview:** it said "Nothing to release." while the real run failed. It now keeps tagged releases in the plan.
- **Older-template tags:** a tag made under an older tag template no longer makes a package look released.
- **Leaky tests:** the tests I wrote contacted a real GitHub URL and sat through 60 seconds of retry sleeps. They now use an offline runner.
- **Left as is (listed in the PR):** a hand-made lightweight tag at HEAD for a finished release now fails with E167 until the next commit. Preview with missing credentials keeps the package planned.

| PR | Work | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #209 | R3: split intent derivation into stages, snapshots first | Open |
| #205, #206, #208 | `init` tests move, workflow templates to files, SYS-NAPI fix | Open, native stack #207 |
| #204 | W0 docs refresh | Open |
| #211 | #202 review fixes | Open |

SYS-NAPI is the one fix the stack carries; it has real-`jq` tests that failed on the old template.

**Not done**
- **SYS-BARRIER:** it goes on top of #209.
- **R1** (`walk.rs`).
- **W1 credential check:** it needs your decision on where it runs in CI.
- **W0 branch deletion:** it needs your per-branch confirmation.

# callisto-cli

## 0.10.3

- A release rerun adopts a local tag whose message has several paragraphs or a signature, instead of failing while reading it.
- A rerun after a failed tag push now completes the release. A tag that exists on the release commit no longer hides unfinished work: the push, GitHub release and any other missing steps are performed and the receipt is written.
- The generated build-matrix release workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release. An unrelated or misconfigured napi addon no longer adds builds or fails the plan job of a release that does not include it.

## 0.10.2

- Releases that ship artifacts no longer fail with E140: the GitHub CLI that checks attestations and publishes the release keeps its own token instead of running unauthenticated.

## 0.10.1

docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:13:| SYS-BARRIER | `release/derive.rs`: a dual Cargo/npm owner creates a shared physical tag/GitHub publication
8:- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. Several identities can currently derive operations addressing the same physical tag or forge release; shared ownership is not yet a separate authority.
9:- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
13:- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.
26:local:  derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
32:- A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed.
66:- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
77:These are version-level checks, not proof of identical bytes, the npm dist-tag, or a full wheel/sdist set. Registry endpoints must be HTTPS. Read-only observations retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines.
98:- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
101:The intended tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package. Derivation currently gates by distribution identity, so one dual Cargo/npm owner's shared tag and public release can precede its other registry publish. This is a contract failure, not a fixed ecosystem order. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.
107:Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect.

# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec: it lists unshipped defects and evidence gaps only. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. No hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run has been performed.

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-OWNER | `sole_owner_at`: current first-manifest path existence is not historic name/full-roster ownership. Reproduced loss of a bare tag after sibling rename or addition of a new primary canonical manifest. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-DEMOTION | `tags.rs`: removing a same-named sibling loses a newer qualified tag and chooses an older bare release. Reproduced; inference can replay already-released work. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-BARRIER | `release/derive.rs`: a dual Cargo/npm owner creates a shared physical tag/GitHub publication after one distribution but before the other's publish. Reproduced plan ordering; per-distribution gates do not enforce the owner's completion barrier. | T08 | REL-ORD-01 |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYFILES | `provider/registry.rs` returns Exact for any matching non-yanked Python file; `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as AlreadySatisfied. `registry_argv.rs` builds both wheel and sdist. Source-confirmed partial-upload retry gap; no live fault-injection run yet. | T09 | REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04 |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

fix(release): tag a Cargo and npm package only after both of its publishes

A package published to both Cargo and npm has one physical tag and GitHub release but a registry publish per manifest. Each release identity's tag waited only for its own publish, so the shared tag and public release could land after the first publish and before the second. A package's tag now waits for the publishes of every release identity it has.

The new test drives the executor's eligibility logic over a derived dual-owner intent: with one publish landed and the other pending, neither the tag, the draft release nor the publication is eligible, in either order. The dual-owner snapshot changes only in the tags' prerequisites and the resulting operation order.

input.content:
SYS-BARRIER (REL-ORD-01). A package published to both Cargo and npm has one physical tag and GitHub release but a registry publish per manifest. Each release identity's tag waited only for its own publish, so the shared tag and public release could land after the first publish and before the second, and a failed second publish left a tagged, announced release.

A package's tag now waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has, through `OpIndex::tag_prerequisites` (introduced by the stage split in #209). The draft release and publication follow the tag, so they inherit the barrier. The order between the ecosystems is still not fixed.

Tests:
- `a_dual_owners_shared_tag_and_release_wait_for_both_registry_publishes` derives a real dual-owner intent and drives the executor's eligibility logic: with one publish landed and the other pending, neither the tag, the draft release nor the publication is eligible, in either order; with both landed the tag is next. It failed before the change.
- The dual-owner snapshot from #209 changes, and only in the tags' prerequisites and the resulting canonical operation order. The other four snapshots are unchanged.

The brief asked for a black-box dual-manifest test with the CLI. The e2e harness has no `npm` fake, so this PR proves the ordering through the production executor logic over a derived intent instead; a harness `npm` fake would let an e2e test also assert that no tag is created when the npm publish fails.

Spec REL-ORD-01, the architecture note and the findings register are updated; changeset for `callisto-cli`. `just ci` passes.

- `discover`: the locator's projects by directory, and the npm platform packages attached to an owner (`Discovered`).
- `assign_identities`: one `IdentityAssigner` that owns the order-dependent bookkeeping (a path's bare versus prefixed id depends on the names seen earlier in path order), with the promotion re-key as a method. The sibling ids a bare name is promoted into are an output of this stage (`Identified`).
- `resolve_packages`: `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` rules, then the zero-match and cross-ecosystem diagnostics.
- `build_edges`: one edge per resolvable dependency declaration.

Moves only. The statements are the original ones; the edits are `self.` prefixes, parameters and borrows. Diagnostics keep their order. content.content:
## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, canonical-only new exact references, registry publication before shared tags/public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. Remaining wire shapes and migration rules below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | The owner chose canonical slash-qualified IDs for every new exact reference; reject new bare and colon-form aliases, and read existing forms only through an explicit ownership migration boundary | Specify which historical records remain readable and how migration is surfaced; cover config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy bare key may resolve to an owner that already has a canonical key in the same file | Choose behavior when both keys carry different versions; current `or_insert` keeps the canonical value and silently drops the migrated legacy value |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | The owner chose required Cargo/npm/PyPI publications before a shared tag and public GitHub release; a future Go source tag can itself be a publication | Specify draft creation and upload ordering and prove all required owner outputs complete before public announcement |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Package owners control hook scripts and any effects they initiate; Callisto preserves native behavior and does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks | Settled owner boundary: preserve it in future publisher changes; do not require hook migration or promise that external hook effects are coordinated |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

content.text:
The 0.10.3 release is fine. Everything left in the plan now needs a decision from you, so I've written a recommendation for each.

Nothing is waiting on code from me. #213 (dual-owner tag barrier) and #214 (`walk.rs` split) are open and clean. #213 can merge now that 0.10.3 is out.

**Recommendations**
1. **W1, where the credential check runs:** add a `callisto-ci.yml` job with `permissions: contents: read` and `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. It downloads the latest release asset with `gh release download` and verifies its attestation. It gets no registry secrets, and the release-workflow policy script stays untouched.
   - Run it on pushes to `main` and same-repo PRs only, because fork PRs get no token.
   - I'd start this first. It's small, and it covers the exact regression behind 0.10.1.
2. **W3, Python partial uploads (SYS-PYFILES):** the required set is every file the build produced.
   - A package counts as satisfied only when each required file is present, not yanked, and has a matching sha256.
   - If files are missing, upload only those.
   - A yanked required file, or a digest mismatch, is a conflict. Never un-yank or overwrite it.
   - That matches how tags and assets already work (REL-RERUN-03).
3. **W4, redacted provider output:**
   - The brief names a `redact_native_output` helper that doesn't exist. The real ones are `redact_known_secrets` and `redact_command_stderr` in `callisto-model`, and both remove known patterns, so a miss leaks.
   - So make `details` a closed enum (exit code, HTTP status, and a fixed set of auth, not-found and conflict kinds) with no free text. Nothing can leak by construction, and the persisted receipt schema stays small.
4. **W10 (smaller decisions):**
   - **Target declarations:** add the `RewriteKey` discriminator so distinct target declarations get their own graph edges. An untracked pin means stale published metadata, the same class as the Cargo-target and extras bugs fixed in 0.10.x. It is a public-API change that `check-api` guards.
   - **Python dev groups:** lean yes, cascade them like Cargo dev-dependencies. This is the shakiest of the five, because dev groups aren't published metadata.
5. **D01, owner contract.** This unblocks W8 (SYS-MATURIN) and W9 (SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION and the resolver divergence). Most rows already have a proposed default in `V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md`. These are the ones that need your call:
   - **Conflicting pre-state aliases:** fail with a typed error naming both keys and both versions. I checked that `PreState::entering` uses `entry().or_insert`, where the first value wins silently. I did not find the exact legacy-versus-canonical merge site, so confirm that before relying on it.
   - **Owner identity:** derive it deterministically from the retained source snapshot, with no persisted ID, and refuse renames until an explicit mapping exists. This avoids a second authority. It is my recommendation, not something I verified.
   - **Wire compatibility:** bump a document's version only when its meaning changes, and reject unsupported old versions with an explicit error.

Say which of these you accept or want changed, and I'll start with W1, then W3 and W4 in the registry provider.

**Housekeeping**
- The W0 branch deletion is still waiting on your per-branch confirmation. The local plan file's W4 brief should be corrected for the missing helper, but background sessions can't edit it.

<pasted_content id="b815">
## Assessment

Claude identified real failure modes, but the recommendations are at different levels of readiness. W1 is a useful CI check with a narrower claim than stated. W3 and D01 need a defined authority and migration contract before implementation. W4 addresses a real leak risk but must cover output paths beyond receipts. W10 contains one concrete identity bug and one policy choice.

### 1. W1 — release attestation check

Verdict: do it, but specify the asset and what the check proves. A job with contents: read and GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} fits the existing CI workflow and keeps registry credentials out. The installer already passes that token and verifies the downloaded asset against the release workflow’s signer identity in install-callisto.sh (.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh:101).

Two claims need correction:

- Fork PRs do receive a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN; they do not receive repository secrets. Restricting this job to same-repo PRs may still be sensible for cost or policy, but “fork PRs get no token” is false. GitHub’s event documentation (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows) states the read-only behavior.
- gh release download without a tag selects the latest release and requires an asset pattern. The job must name the expected platform asset and verify it with --repo and --signer-workflow. It will test the currently selected release and CI token access, not prove every historical release or the full installer fallback path. GitHub CLI download (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_download) and attestation verification (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify) document those boundaries.

I would run the job on main pushes and same-repo PRs as proposed, then record an intentional behavior for a repository with no suitable release. The release-workflow policy script can stay untouched; the CI workflow contract checks should still be run.

### 2. W3 — Python partial uploads

Verdict: correct completion rule, incomplete execution design. The defect is supported: one matching non-yanked file currently yields Exact in registry.rs (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs:574), while the publisher builds a wheel and sdist and uploads a broad glob in registry_argv.rs (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs:334).

“Every file the build produced” raises the decisive question: which build, and where is its trusted inventory retained for a retry? The current publisher rebuilds inside the effect, then uploads from dist/. It does not bind that output set and its hashes to the sealed release intent. Rebuilding after a partial upload could produce different bytes; observing the new build as the required set would silently change the release target. The current dist/ glob also does not itself prove that every selected file came from this invocation.

The safe sequence is to declare selected outputs, build into an isolated location, record exact filenames and hashes in a trusted artifact inventory bound to the run, then observe each required file before selecting only missing files for upload. A yanked required file or mismatched hash should block. The plan must define local retry retention and index lag behavior. Its comparison to tags/assets is directionally useful, but REL-RERUN-03 (docs/specs/release.json:245) does not already specify Python file-set proof.

### 3. W4 — redacted provider output

Verdict: prefer closed structured details, but scope the leak paths first. Claude’s correction is sound: redact_native_output does not exist, and redact_known_secrets (crates/callisto-model/src/registry.rs:114) can only replace secrets it knows. A closed enum for persisted diagnostic details removes free-text credential exposure from that field.

There is an important scope distinction: provider observations are already closed enums in release_observation.rs (crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs:80). Free-text error fields and subprocess stderr remain elsewhere, and the CLI runner can print redacted native output. Changing a receipt detail type alone would not establish “nothing can leak by construction.” Inventory every path from provider stdout/stderr into errors, live logs, summaries and persisted files; use closed data wherever Callisto owns the diagnostic. Keep native stderr handling as a separate, explicitly limited boundary.

The proposed enum also needs enough fixed cases to distinguish an authentication failure from a transport failure or malformed response without accidentally reporting either as an absent remote object.

### 4. W10 — target declarations and Python dev groups

Target declarations: accept the defect, challenge the size estimate. RewriteKey (crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:576) distinguishes manifest, name and dependency kind, but no target table. Cargo extraction and rewriting currently walk top-level dependency sections in cargo.rs (crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:398). A discriminator on RewriteKey alone cannot recover target declarations that were never emitted as edges, nor can the existing writer address their table. The fix needs a declaration locator carried through extraction, graph edges, cascade, snapshot and the format-preserving writer. Review public constructors and check-api together. This is a justified correction, but it is not merely one added key field.

Python dev groups: defer the “yes” pending an owner choice. python.rs (crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:459) reads published runtime dependencies and Poetry dependencies, but no dev groups. Cargo’s existing rule rewrites dev constraints without bumping the dependent; that is a plausible policy for Python groups, not evidence that users expect every local tooling group to participate in release versioning. Define which group formats are supported, how includes and duplicate declarations work, and whether stale pins are release errors before making this a gate.

### 5. D01 — owner contract

Conflicting pre-state aliases: accept, and the merge site is confirmed. assign_promoted_pre_keys (crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:275) resolves keys, removes a legacy key and calls entry(owner_key).or_insert(version) at line 338.
